newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai 1997 GDP growth seen steady at 6.2-6.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: Thai 1997 GDP growth seen steady at 6.2-6.9 pct.

text.p: Siam Commercial Bank Plc forecast on Monday that Thai economic growth this year would be relatively steady from 1996, but that the current account deficit and inflation would likely ease.
Olarn Chaipravat, the president of Siam Commercial Bank, said that he expected the Thai gross domesic product to expand 6.2-6.9 percent against 6.7 posted in 1996.
He forecast that Thai exports would turn more robust, growing about 7.0-10.0 percent over 1996 after a dismal 0.2 percent contraction a year ago.
Olarn said the current account deficit, helped by improving exports, would likely narrow to 7.1-7.8 percent of GDP in 1997 from 8.0 in 1996.
He said inflation would also slow to about 4.0 percent from 5.9 percent last year.
The head of the Thai Bankers Association warned Thailand still needs to focus on improving its economic fundamentals despite the slightly better 1997 outlook.
He said the authorities should continue monitoring the import of short-term capital and curb excessive imports.
